intro: Lesson 60: Polygon problems and tessellation. To understand how polygon angle facts solve problems, including which regular polygons tessellate

model.title: A regular pentagon and a regular hexagon share a side. Find the angle between them at a shared vertex.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Angles at a point add up to 360°

questions.q: Two regular octagons and one other regular polygon meet at a point with no gap. What is the other polygon?
questions.model: 2 × 135 = 270. 360 - 270 = 90°, the interior angle of a square.

questions.q: Two regular hexagons and one other regular polygon meet at a point. What is the third?
The interior angle of a regular 12-gon

(a) Explain with angles why regular octagons do not tessellate alone. (b) Two regular 12-gons and one other regular polygon meet at a point: which one? (c) A regular hexagon and a square share a side: find the angle between them at a shared vertex. (d) A square, a regular hexagon and a regular 12-gon meet at a point: do they fit exactly?
questions.a: (a) 2 × 135 = 270 leaves a gap; 3 × 135 = 405 overlaps (b) an equilateral triangle (c) 150° (d) yes: 90 + 120 + 150 = 360°
questions.model: (a) 360 ÷ 135 = 2.67, not a whole number, so octagons alone leave gaps. (b) 2 × 150 = 300; 360 - 300 = 60°: an equilateral triangle.

questions.q: In regular pentagon ABCDE, find angle BAC.
questions.a: Triangle ABC is isosceles with angle B = 108°, so BAC = (180 - 108) ÷ 2 = 36°

questions.q: Explain why only three regular polygons tessellate on their own.
questions.a: The interior angle must divide 360°. It is at least 60° and less than 180°, so only 60°, 90° and 120° work: triangle, square and hexagon.

questions.q: Why do regular pentagons not tessellate?
options: they have an odd number of sides

questions.q: Square + two octagons at a point add up to
Big question: which regular polygons tile a floor alone, and why?
questions.a: Triangles, squares and hexagons: their interior angles (60°, 90°, 120°) divide 360° exactly.
